Position & Pleadings
1.

This petition U/s 166 r/w Section 140 of M.V. Act was filed on 22/03/2023 seeking compensation
in respect of the death of one Sh. Prakash Pathak S/o Sh. Ganesh Pathak
(hereinafter referred to as "deceased") due to a motor vehicular accident dated 22/03/2023.

As per petition, the accident had taken place on 23/11/2022 at about 11.19 PM, when the deceased came under the vehicle and struck bearing registration no. DL-5GQ-8927 (hereinafter referred to as "offending vehicle") as the said vehicle was parked on the slope without safety of hand break and the said vehicle bearing registration no. DL-5GQ-8927 was slopped and deceased struck under the said vehicle.

It is further stated that the deceased was struck under the vehicle bearing registration no. DL-5GQ-8927 due to negligence on the part of R-1 as the R-1 has parked his above vehicle on the slope without following safety rules, as the vehicle was parked without hand break on the slope/ rame and when the deceased stood in front of the vehicle then the said vehicle suddenly started rollling down and the deceased unable to stop the vehicle due to sudden rolling down vehicle the deceased struck under vehicle and found dead.
As per petition, the deceased was 32 years old, was doing a private job and was earning Rs.32,000/- per month.
Petitioner seeks compensation to the tune of Rs. 90 Lakhs in respect of the untimely death of deceased in the abovesaid accident.
An FIR no. 560/22 PS Subzi Mandi U/s 279/304A IPC was registered in respect of the above accident.
R-1 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
R-2 is the driver of the offending vehicle and R-3 is the insurer of the same.
Notice of this petition was issued to all the MACT No. 220/23 Archana Pathak & Ors Vs. Sadanand Pathak & Ors.

In support of their contentions, the petitioners examined Petitioner No. 1 Smt. Archana, wife of the deceased, as PW-1.
PW-1, vide her affidavit Ex. PW1/A deposed that the deceased lost his life on 23.11.2022 due to an accident involving the offending vehicle.
She further deposed that the accident took place due to the rashness and negligence of R-1.
She further deposed that the deceased was 32 years old, was doing a private job and was earning a sum of Rs. 32,000/- per month from his job.
She further deposed that the petitioners, being the wife, children and mother of the deceased, were completely dependent on the earnings of the deceased.
5.1 PW1 was cross-examined by Ld. Counsel for R-2/ Insurance Company Only.

In her cross-examination she deposed that she is not an eye witness to the accident and she came to know about the accident after some time by Sadanand Pathak (respondent no. 1) and Sh. Sadanand Pathak is elder brother of her deceased husband.
She denied the suggestion that deceased was not earning Rs.32,000/- per month at the relevant time.
She further denied the suggestion that she has filed the present claim petition in collusion with respondent no. 1.
She further denied the suggestion that she is not entitled to any compensation owing the said fact.

In the present matter, the police filed a cancellation report after registration of instant FIR on the premise that the deceased came under the wheels of his own car as he tried to stop the Car which started moving on a sloppy road.
There is no challenge of the said cancellation report before Ld. MM by the petitioners.
Further, the ignition key was recovered from the pocket of the deceased.
The iron angle near the front tyre pierced the back of the deceased and caused his death.
9.1 The DAR was closed by Ld. Predecessor of this Tribunal after due consideration.
Thereafter, the petitioners filed the separate petition u/s 164 MV Act which was amended to petition u/s 166 MV Act.
The evidence of R2W1 is important as in his evidence he reiterated the same facts as stated in the DAR.
His testimony would show that while he reached the spot of accident he found that the deceased was lying trapped under the car of make Hyundai Venue and the ignition key was found in his pocket.

He further stated that upon enquiry, one of the bystander told him that the car was standing on a slope at the place of accident and while the deceased was trying to stop it, the deceased came beneath of the said car.

As per petition, the accident had taken place on 23/11/2022 at about 11.19 PM, when the deceased came under the vehicle and struck bearing registration no. DL-5GQ-8927 (hereinafter referred to as "offending vehicle") as the said vehicle was parked on the slope without safety of hand break and the said vehicle bearing registration no. DL-5GQ-8927 was slopped and deceased struck under the said vehicle.
It is further stated that the deceased was struck under the vehicle bearing registration no. DL-5GQ-8927 due to negligence on the part of R-1 as the R-1 has parked his above vehicle on the slope without following safety rules, as the vehicle was parked without hand break on the slope/ rame and when the deceased stood in front of the vehicle then the said vehicle suddenly started rollling down and the deceased unable to stop the vehicle due to sudden rolling down vehicle the deceased struck under vehicle and found dead.
In the present matter, the police filed a cancellation report after registration of instant FIR on the premise that the deceased came under the wheels of his own car as he tried to stop the Car which started moving on a sloppy road.
There is no challenge of the said cancellation report before Ld. MM by the petitioners.
Further, the ignition key was recovered from the pocket of the deceased.
The iron angle near the front tyre pierced the back of the deceased and caused his death.
9.1 The DAR was closed by Ld. Predecessor of this Tribunal after due consideration.
Thereafter, the petitioners filed the separate petition u/s 164 MV Act which was amended to petition u/s 166 MV Act.
His testimony would show that while he reached the spot of accident he found that the deceased was lying trapped under the car of make Hyundai Venue and the ignition key was found in his pocket.
He further stated that upon enquiry, one of the bystander told him that the car was standing on a slope at the place of accident and while the deceased was trying to stop it, the deceased came beneath of the said car.
Therefore, this issue is decided against the petitioners and in favour of the respondents.
